description: This course examines how American cinema has imagined petroleum as a means to and an object of desire; a source of mobility, masculinity, wealth, sex, racial and national power—and of course, catastrophe. Students learn the fundamentals of film analysis while tracing the cultural history of fossil fuel through melodrama, documentary, propaganda, blockbuster, horror, animation, independent cinema, and so on. We combine close, critical analysis with some creative filmmaking exercises, all revolving around the strange question: How has oil taught Americans to love? Offered periodically during spring semester.
name: Love and Oil in American Cinema
